campaign: MOSS in overgo does what the MOSS Ultra workflow does in ComfyUI, each section held to ComfyUI's recording

items.title: A browser wait that cannot come true fails when the page is idle, saying what the page shows, in every run

steps.title: A browser wait ends when the page is idle and its predicate false, with what the page shows; no clock ends it
steps.rationale:
The owner's review of 2026-11-24 (third), cause 3, checked against the code: valid. Browser.Eventually (internal/webuilane/browser.go:254) waits until its predicate holds, with no end but a budget the user sets, so a predicate a change makes unsatisfiable holds the lane: four hangs on 2026-11-24 (moss-page/pictures' undo run 32 min, a faults leg on a mutation loop, a restored-settings leg on a refused run, a full lane 20 min on TestWebUIBrowserArtifactLinks' changed title), and a verbose rerun was needed to learn which.

Pages do keep work open for good, which the rule must read: the activity stream (/runtime/activity/stream, workflow.js connect) stays open while subscribed, and intervals poll for the page's life (boot.js statusRefresh and the offline probe, requests.js refresh, runtime.js monitor). So idle is: no shell request in flight besides the stream (api.inFlight), no one-shot timer pending, and each interval fired since the page last changed; then a false predicate ends the wait as failed, with the page's ready state, panels and last error, as Eventually reports them now.

Check: TestWebUIBrowserAWaitThatCannotComeTrueFailsWhenIdle waits on a predicate that never holds on a page holding the stream and its intervals, and finds the wait failed with the page's state, while a wait on a predicate a pending request makes true still passes. It does not exist at the base, so the check fails there (the lane fails it as an unfinished leg).

items.title: A check's pass is kept while what it read is unchanged, its inputs observed, so a commit runs only the checks its change can alter

steps.title: Each commit's checks are measured for what they read and why go test's cache does not keep them
steps.rationale: The owner's review of 2026-11-24 (third), cause 1, checked against the code and a measurement: valid. The cycle lanes run go test -count=1 (internal/landing/lanes.go:150), since go test's cache keys a pass by what it opened only where it can see it, so a page commit reruns the 2,404 model tests; and internal/landing, untouched by any moss-page commit, ran in full (148 s) in each one's invariants stage. Measured: two runs of go test ./internal/landing with nothing changed between them both ran in full (110 s), the first's result unkept. The change: a package's test run (testevidence) records what its test binary opened, from the binary's own test log (-test.testlogfile), each file by its content, and names it; this step reports, for internal/landing and the lanes' packages, what they read and which input moves at each commit. Check: TestAPackageRunNamesWhatItRead runs a fixture package whose test opens one file and finds that file named with its content's digest.

steps.title: The gate and the lanes keep a package's pass while its test binary and every file it read are unchanged by content
steps.rationale: Follows observed-inputs/measure. The change: one rule for every test the gate's stages and the lanes run. A package's pass is kept, by its test binary's identity and the digests of what it read, and a later run whose binary and inputs match takes the kept pass in place of running; any input that differs runs it. Declared inputs and -count=1 go. Check: TestAPassIsKeptWhileWhatItReadIsUnchanged runs a fixture package twice and finds the second taken from the kept pass, then changes the file it reads and finds it run. It does not exist at the base, so the check fails there.

steps.title: The mechanisms the kept passes make redundant go: the yield to a newer commit, the lanes' rotation and the per-package turn handover
steps.rationale: Follows observed-inputs/rule. With passes kept by what they read, a run at an older commit spends nothing a newer one repeats, so the run's yield to a newer commit due (plan.Yields, cmd/validate/run.go:276) goes; the lanes need no rotation to reach packages long without a pass (lanes-rotation, which this step retires unworked); and the per-package handover of the test turn (testSteps, landing.HoldTestTurnEach) stays only where a package's own run outlasts a commit's patience, which turn-priority covers. Check: TestNoLaneYieldsOrRotatesWhatAKeptPassCovers finds no yield and no rotation in a lanes run whose packages' passes are kept. It does not exist at the base, so the check fails there.

items.title: A rerun without the change that outlasts twice the check's own time is said for every kind of check, a browser lane's and a pipeline's among them

steps.title: A check that runs no go test of its own is timed for the overrun notice from its start
steps.rationale:
The owner's review of 2026-11-24, point 1, checked against the code: valid. The undo run's overrun notice (internal/landing/undo.go overrunClock) starts when began is called, and planverify calls began only on a go test JSON start event (progressLines.show). A check run through cmd/webui-lane prints its own lines, so for a browser check the notice never starts: moss-page/pictures' first attempt hung 32 minutes in its undo run on 2026-11-24, and nothing said so; the same hang went unsaid on 2026-11-22. TestACheckShowsItsProgress asserts the gap: a command running no test binary is said to begin none.

The change: ExecuteShowing calls began as it starts a check whose parse names no go test of its own (a browser lane, a pipeline over validate), so its overrun is timed from its start, its build included, as its wall with the change was; a go test check keeps its clock from its first test binary's start (undo-overrun/do). TestACheckShowsItsProgress's last case is replaced.

Check: TestACheckRunningNoGoTestIsTimedFromItsStart runs a command that runs no go test (go version) and finds began called once, as it starts, and a go test check's began still called as each test binary starts. It does not exist at the base, so the check fails there.

items.title: A turn that asks only for a status answer ends with it; a decision that changes a standing rule waits for the next turn that implements

steps.title: The stop hook lets a clean, typed status turn end though a doctrine decision waits
steps.rationale: SQA-490, checked against the code at db04fec59: valid from source. runStop (cmd/loophook/main.go) calls answerHold before it uses stopDecision's verdict, so a typed turn that asks only for status, with the tree clean and no landing running, is held to answer a doctrine decision first (exit 2). The hold came with doctrine-answer (528f40b3f) after an eight-hour wait on such a decision; the wait it cures is an unattended or implementing turn that ends on the decision, not a status answer. The change: answerHold holds a turn only where stopDecision would hold it for its work (an implementing turn, or one whose tree or landing is unfinished); a clean typed turn ends, the decision staying in Dispatch.Answer for the next. Check: TestAStatusTurnEndsThoughADecisionWaits runs the hook on a clean typed turn with a doctrine decision waiting and finds it let end, and on an implementing turn finds it held. It does not exist at the base, so the check fails there.

items.title: A pause the owner asks for is recorded by the session it was asked of, and another session's prompt in the checkout neither grants nor withdraws it

steps.title: The stop request is the asking session's, not the checkout's latest prompt
steps.rationale: SQA-487, checked against the code at 30691fc67: valid from source. runPrompt (cmd/loophook/main.go) calls NoteStopRequest for every session's prompt before it reads who holds the worktree, and both sessions write or remove the one stop_request file, so a review session's progress question removes the lead's request before RecordStop reads it; and the stop words are tested by containment, so "don't stop" reads as a request. The change: the request is kept per session (its session id), only the worktree holder's session records it, and a negated stop word is no request. Check: TestAStopRequestIsTheAskingSessions notes a request in one session, a progress prompt in another, and finds the first's request standing for its RecordStop and "don't stop" no request. It does not exist at the base, so the check fails there.

items.title: The review ratchet vetoes what a reader cannot see past, not a nested ternary a line break hides

steps.title: The nested-ternary count leaves the landing's veto
steps.rationale: SQA-488, checked against the code at 30691fc67: valid. The review ratchet (internal/webuilane review_test.go) counts a nested ternary only within one physical line, so a line break after the outer question mark passes the same expression; it refused three landings (moss-sharpened-pair/do, moss-sharpened-pair/page, moss-page/pictures) whose other counts were zero, each cured by reflowing or naming the inner choice. A count a line break defeats is no rule. The change: removing the nested-ternary counter, its ceiling and its fixture expectation; readability stays with review, and the ratchet's other counts stand. Check: TestTheReviewRatchetCountsNoNestedTernary reviews a fixture holding a one-line nested ternary and finds the ratchet's report holds no such count. It does not exist at the base, so the check fails there.

items.title: A check is filed as the shell runs it: an assignment of a command's output runs that command, and the literal false, which no work can pass, is refused

steps.title: A check is filed as the shell runs it: an assignment of a command's output runs that command, and the literal false, which no work can pass, is refused
steps.rationale:
SQA-482 and SQA-483, checked against the code at 5f5d4db92: both valid.

SQA-482: verifyRefusal (cmd/plan/main.go) files the literal false, and TestACheckThatCannotRunAsWrittenIsRefusedWhenFiled lists it among the checks a step may take. A step filed with false fails at its commit whatever the work, so measured-names-first/do, contended-credit/do, user-size-inapplicable/do and flash-next-projection/do were each retired and the work landed under another step. The change: verifyRefusal refuses a check that is only false, saying to name the test the change will add (the commit's form stage finds it by go test -list once written).

SQA-483: ParseVerify (internal/runrecord/verify_command.go) splits s=$(go run ./cmd/validate -scorecard) at the parenthesis and refuses the segment s=$ as one that sets an environment and runs nothing, though the shell runs the command it captures. The refusal stands in a plain && chain, where an assignment alone exports nothing to the commands after it; in a composite command, which the shell runs whole and which no caller reads for cached credit, a segment of assignments alone is the shell's own form and is kept. The full-measurement/run check written that way was refused at its commit after nine hours of measurement.

Check: TestACheckNoWorkCanPassIsRefusedWhenFiled files false and is refused; TestAnAssignmentOfACommandsOutputRunsIt parses the original full-measurement/run check as composite, with no error, and still refuses A=1 && go test as a plain chain. Neither test exists at the base, so the check fails there.

items.title: A measurement cycle answers with the scorecard it published, so a cycle cut short at a commit another cycle published keeps its cells and files no gaps of the other's

steps.title: A measurement cycle answers with the scorecard it published, so a cycle cut short at a commit another cycle published keeps its cells and files no gaps of the other's
steps.rationale:
SQA-474 (as the review wrote it at a25fa2246), checked against the code at 5f5d4db92: valid from source. improvement.Measure (cmd/loop/improve.go) returns the newest scorecard record when its commit is the cycle's, whoever published it; a cycle whose lane fails before it publishes, at a commit an earlier cycle published, so answers with the earlier record. Improve (internal/loop/driver.go) then files that record's gaps and runs Fill, whose deferred removals take cycle_state.json and cycle_credit.json, so the cells this cycle finished are measured again by the next. Not observed: the unattended cycle has not run since the measurements moved to validate -run phases.

The change: Measure answers with a record only when this cycle's publication ran (the published callback measureScorecard calls); otherwise it returns the lane's error with no record, and the state and credit stay for the resume.

Check: TestACycleCutShortAnswersWithNoScorecardItDidNotPublish holds a published record at the commit, fails a lane before publication, and finds no record answered, no gaps filed and the credit file kept. It does not exist at the base, so the check fails there.

items.title: A lanes run that yields to a newer commit keeps its place: the next takes first the packages longest without a pass that still holds, so every lane runs whole within one rotation while commits arrive

steps.title: A lanes run that yields to a newer commit keeps its place: the next takes first the packages longest without a pass that still holds, so every lane runs whole within one rotation while commits arrive
steps.rationale: The owner's review of 2026-11-23, point 3, checked against cmd/validate/run.go and .overgo-runtime/lanes.log: valid. A cycle's lanes run in one order (model-journey, audio, models, needle-reference, sequences); as a lane turns to another package the run yields to a newer commit due (lanes-first/yield), and every lane after the one yielding does not run. A row closes every 30 to 40 minutes and models takes hours, so each run yields inside models (lanes.log: 635db11e9, aaba3c348, 08a0ad2c7, e30533414, b17937206 each 'yields to ... as it turns to another package'), needle-reference and sequences have not run since 22 Nov 07:15, and the models lane has not passed whole for 28 commits; a run starts each time at the first lane again, so the packages it never reaches are the same ones. The change: a package's pass is kept with the commit it ran at, and holds at a later commit whose changes do not reach it (the lanes' readers by path, CycleLanesReached); a run, after the checks the commit's change names (lanes-first), takes the packages longest without a pass that holds, across lanes, so a yield loses nothing and the next run goes on where it stopped; a lane is whole where every package has a pass that holds at the commit read, and validate says the oldest pass any lane relies on. Check: TestAYieldedLanesRunResumesItsRotation runs stand-in lanes yielding after each package as commits arrive: every package of every lane runs within one rotation, a package a later commit reaches runs again, and the lanes read whole once each has a pass that holds.

items.title: The MOSS golden floors are read before a section is drawn and refuse a reference of no signal, and the sharpened pair's check compares pixels

steps.title: The sharpened pair's check compares the pictures' pixels, so a finishing that changes none is refused
steps.rationale: SQA-467 (P2: a check that passes without checking), checked against sharpened_pair_windows_test.go at 47b3587c9: valid. The test strips the pictures' texts before it holds the drawn picture equal to the plain one, but holds the finished picture apart from the unsharpened one by their PNG bytes, and only the finished PNG carries Finishing=sharpened, so a finishing that returned its input's pixels would pass. The change: the inequality compares decoded pixels, the drawn-equals-plain comparison as it is. Check: the test itself, which a finishing that changes no pixel now fails.

steps.title: The MOSS golden floors are declared before a section is drawn, each failed comparison is reported and its generator closed, and a reference of no signal is refused
steps.rationale: SQA-410 (P2), checked against golden_floor_windows_model_test.go and decibelsOverSquares at 47b3587c9: valid. holdGoldenFloors draws every case (readGoldenCases) before it asks whether each declares a floor, so a missing declaration costs five baseline draws and five controls; a later case's size error stops the test before an earlier failure is reported or the open generator closed; each control encodes a PNG it throws away; and a reference of all zeros scores -Inf in both precision modes, which holdMergedSections accepts as equal. The change: floors are checked before any draw, a comparison's failure is reported as it is scored and its generator closed by Cleanup, a control keeps its latent alone, and decibelsOverSquares refuses a reference with no signal while agreement with a nonzero one stays +Inf. Check: the floors test itself, with card-free cases for the refusals where they need no draw.

items.title: The workflow clock refuses a record it cannot write before it draws, and a ComfyUI recording binds each output to what made it

steps.title: The workflow clock refuses a record path that is not relative to the repository before it holds the machine or draws a section
steps.rationale:
SQA-460 (P2), checked against readWorkflowSource and appendWorkflowTiming at 47b3587c9: valid. An absolute OVERGO_WORKFLOW_RECORD is accepted at the start and joined under the repository only when the timing is appended, after both runs, so the attempt reported in d28ab1e84 drew twelve sections (81 s measured) and saved nothing. The change: the record path is checked, relative and inside the repository, before the quiet machine is asked for. Check: TestTheWorkflowClockRefusesARecordItCannotWrite gives the source check an absolute path and one leaving the repository: each is refused before any draw.

Note: SQA-477 (P2), valid from source: ownSizeReading and TestWhereAMossStepsTimeGoes divide a recording's elapsed time by its count of progress-event intervals, not by the steps between its first and last event, so a recording with a gap in its step numbers reads slow (1.113 against 1.136 s/step with one interior event dropped; node 48 of a Turbo capture records steps 1 to 8 in five events, 129.75 against 74.14 ms/step). The intact own-size recording has all 50 events, so no reading taken so far is wrong. With this step: the MOSS recording reader computes time per completed step from the first and last timestamps and their step numbers, both timing checks read it before loading the generator, and a span of fewer than two events is refused there.

steps.title: A ComfyUI recording binds a resumed output to the prompt that made it, keeps two files of one name apart, and credits a repeat only from two prompts
steps.rationale: SQA-388 (P2), checked against cmd/comfy-reference/record.go at 47b3587c9: valid. record resumes a prompt on its request hash and prompt ID alone after reading the current models and commits; await starts sampling memory at a retry; keep names a file by its node and base name, so two files of one name from one node in different subfolders overwrite each other; and the paired-recording check asks each run for a prompt ID but never compares them, so one capture given twice passes as two runs. The three pairs at 89cf0f0e3 have distinct prompt IDs. The change: a resumed output keeps the producer it was recorded under and is refused when the models or commits moved; memory sampling begun on a retry says so; a kept file's name holds its subfolder; and a pair's prompt IDs differ. Check: TestARecordingBindsEachOutputToWhatMadeIt drives record against a stand-in ComfyUI for each case.

items.title: Every served path's request is split into its parts, each with its wall, processor time and bytes read, as the MOSS workflow's clock reads them, so time outside the model shows on each

steps.title: Every served path's request is split into its parts, each with its wall, processor time and bytes read, as the MOSS workflow's clock reads them, so time outside the model shows on each
steps.rationale:
The owner's review of 2026-11-22 (second), point 3, checked against the code: partly valid. The parts ledger exists for every served path (processmeasure.Stages): the session director marks the request read, the stored answer sought, the named inputs read, the session leased and the run recorded, the workflow runtime marks each stage by its module, video marks its own (prompt rows, denoising, decoding, the clip written) and chat its load's (cmd/recipe inference_measure). But a part records its wall and the device's peak alone, speech marks none of its own, and only the MOSS workflow's clock reads a request's parts beside each one's processor time and bytes read (latentimage TestTheUltraWorkflowIsTimedInItsOrder, readProcessUse, written into that test), which is how adapter-hold's per-request hashing was found.

The change: a part records its processor time and the bytes the process read inside it (processmeasure.Part), so every ledger carries what the MOSS clock computed by hand; speech marks its parts as video does; and the recipe command's measure reports every served task's parts, not chat's load alone. The MOSS clock reads the ledger in place of its own counters.

Check: TestEachServedPathSplitsItsRequestIntoParts serves a picture, a clip, speech and a chat turn through their capabilities with stand-in sessions under a ledger: each request's parts name its load or lease, its stages and its recording, each with wall, processor time and bytes read, their walls inside the request's.

Note: SQA-468 (P3) and the generator part of SQA-461 go with this step, as the parts they cost show in its ledger: the finished PNG is rebuilt with its texts by the workflow's output encoder, keptDrawn and the workspace's OutputContent though the generator wrote them once (three full rewrites a fresh draw, two a repeat, withPictureTexts allocating a whole buffer even where every chunk matches), and Generator.Reset and prepare each open model_index.json again on a changed seed. Where the ledger shows them, PNGContent keeps bytes already carrying the texts it would write, the artifact ID unchanged, and the catalog is read once a session.

Note: SQA-471 (P2) goes with this step, checked against the clock's decode split at 7fbcacc4c: valid. The clock reads its parts by time.Now and the decode's own parts from processmeasure.Stages, two clocks, so the first decode's four parts summed to 426 ms inside its 418 ms; the decode's parts record zero processor time and bytes read, unmeasured, as if measured; and "decoder compiled" holds compileResidentStatic's binding of every static input as well as the compile. The parts are read on the ledger's one clock, enclosing interval and its exclusive parts, processor time and bytes read written only where measured, and the compile and the static binding named apart or together as what they are, before the decoder's 0.47 s is cured.

Note: SQA-473 (P2), valid from source: sliceLastTemporalTap copies a VAE kernel whose temporal extent is 1 whole (97.0 MB at MOSS's decoder load), and VAEProgram.feeds keeps 108.9 MB of host weights after the resident decoder has bound them (decoder-resident). No wall is measured. This step's parts of the first run (46.4 s against ComfyUI's 40.2 s) decide whether the copy and the kept feeds earn a step: the copy can return the weight itself when the kernel has one temporal tap, and the generator can release its feeds once the decoder holds them, keeping them on a failed bind.

items.title: SenseNova's request-resources test is measured again on a card to itself and carries modeltest, so the gate's cuda lane runs no real-model test

steps.title: SenseNova's request-resources test is measured again on a card to itself and carries modeltest, so the gate's cuda lane runs no real-model test
steps.rationale:
The evidence: cuda-synthetic/tag moved every untagged CUDA test that reads the data root behind modeltest but one. TestSenseNovaVariableRequestResources runs SenseNova's 8B production generation in an isolated measurement process, and docs/image_video_capacity.json names its retained measurement by the bytes of its file (evidence:sha256:888854b5...), which the store holds; tagged, its bytes changed and TestImageVideoCapacityAcceptance found no evidence under the new identity. A measurement is taken again only on a card to itself, and the readings campaign holds the card until its Wan arms are drawn, so the file stays in the gate, named by the check as measuredInPlace, and this row follows the campaign.

The change: the test carries //go:build modeltest, it is measured again on a quiet card into the store, the capacity record and its protocol digest (imageVideoCapacitySHA256) name the new identity, and measuredInPlace goes, so internal/sensenovarecipe leaves the cuda lane.

Check: a whole-tree test with measuredInPlace gone, named afresh so it fails before the change: TestTheGateRunsNoRealModelTest.

Refiled 2026-11-16 from cuda-resources/do, whose step carried no card need, so dispatch gave it while the readings campaign held the card: this step carries -needs-card and waits for a card to itself.

items.title: The README shows what LiveEdit does: a source clip and its edit side by side at the editor's own size, with the instruction, as the other models show theirs

steps.title: The README's LiveEdit sample is a source clip and its edit at 832 x 480 side by side, the instruction stated, its time its own run's
steps.rationale: The owner's review of 2026-11-24 (fourth), checked against the README and the code: valid. The README's LiveEdit line links a 32 x 16 clip of 21 frames, states no instruction, shows no source clip, and says 9.5 s where the scorecard table says 10.2 s (the line's own run, not the scorecard's). The editor was trained at 832 x 480 (internal/latentvideo/edit_profiles.json source_width and source_height), and EditSourceSize (edit_form.go:103) says that at a quarter of that size it changes texture, not what the instruction asks; readme-media redid SenseNova, Un-0 and Wan and left LiveEdit. The change: a source clip at 832 x 480 (one of the VidGen clips the edit suite reads) edited by an instruction through go run ./cmd/recipe run -fresh, the source and the edit drawn side by side in one GIF, its caption naming the instruction, the seed, the frames and steps and the run's own time and memory, as the other models' samples are; the earlier clip and its file go. Check: the earlier clip is no longer linked, and the README's tests (repoanalysis, commanddoc) pass, among them TestReadmeNamesEveryModelAndItsSamples.

items.title: Un-0 learns pictures: its trainer fits each class's pictures, a checkpoint trained on 8x8 handwritten digits stands beside the bootstrap one, and the README shows what it draws

steps.title: The Un-0 trainer fits each class's pictures: each step draws one picture per class and takes its squared error against a picture of that class from a dataset
steps.rationale:
The owner, 2026-11-24: the README's Un-0 card suggests Un-0 is not working. Checked: the port is right (its operators and its four-step generator match the reference within 1e-4 and 1e-3, the un0 goldens), but the checkpoint never learned a picture. Its weights are spread like a fresh start (conv weights with a standard deviation of 0.08 to 0.11, biases within 0.82), and the only objective its trainer has, classTargetLoss (internal/oscillatorimage/trainer.go), pulls every pixel of class c to the flat level 0.1 + 0.2c, which tanh and the 0-255 mapping show as three near-greys, the card's colourless noise. So no draw of it can be a better picture; a trained one can.

The change: the trainer takes a picture objective beside the class target. Each step draws one picture per class from random phases and takes the squared error against a picture of that class drawn from a dataset (its pixels in [-1, 1] as tanh gives them), so the generator learns each class's mean picture, a legible one at 8 x 8. cmd/train's oscillatorimage route takes the dataset and writes the trained weights beside a config, as a new model directory; the bootstrap Un-0 is kept.

Check: TestUn0LearnsItsClassesPictures trains a bootstrap model on three synthetic 8 x 8 classes (a ring, a bar, a cross): the loss falls by half or more, and each class's draws are nearer their own class's mean than another's. It does not exist at the base, so the check fails there.

Next, once the owner allows the download of the UCI optdigits data (8 x 8 handwritten digits, about 0.5 MB, from archive.ics.uci.edu): a step that trains Un-0 on the digits 0, 1 and 2, and the README's card of the trained checkpoint, which serves as Un-0 only on the owner's answer (activating a model).

decisions.question: skill.md's 227 rule lines each cite a check. Read at 3ba4de8c7: the first check of 181 has a doc comment and of 45 has none, and the comments state what their test holds, not the rule that cites it ("purpose = recursive self-improvement ..." cites TestCycleFilesDeclinesAndAcceptsNothing, whose comment is the cycle's comparisons; "scorecard columns = ..." cites TestScorecardRowsEveryServableModel, whose comment is rows and dashes). Writing skill.md from the comments as they stand changes what it says. Which form does skill.md take?
options: Each rule line moves onto its first check as a doc-comment line of its own, and skill.md is generated from those lines and its judgement section, so it says what it says now, each rule written once on its check
skill.md holds its terms and judgement lines alone; the rule lines go, each check saying its rule when it refuses
skill.md is written from the tests' doc comments as they stand, its wording changing to theirs
decisions.recommendation: Each rule line moves onto its first check as a doc-comment line of its own, and skill.md is generated from those lines and its judgement section, so it says what it says now, each rule written once on its check
